There are partial-depth ingress and egress points (Gaia 0.93 one field-of-view transit after a 0.69 epoch; ZTF r 0.93 about 0.06 d after 0.73), so the eclipse lasts a few hours. That fits 2R/v for solar-type stars at P about 1.5-3 d. The true period may be 3 d with two equal eclipses, which would explain why no secondary is found. The star is quiet outside eclipse, contamination is negligible, and the coincidence test is null.

explanation: A detached eclipsing binary with P = 25.34 d. The Gaia dip at t = 235.5-235.8 is about 23% deep, grey (RP/BP depth ratio 1.02) and appears in both fields of view with a resolved ingress. ZTF dips of similar depth at 1451.8 (g and r together), 1527.8, 2946.7 (i) and 3934.9 (r) all phase to within about 0.01 cycles of that ephemeris. Recurrence aligns 5 of 6 events with purity 1.0. The sixth event, at ztf_g 2961.8 (phase about 0.6), may be an eccentric secondary eclipse or a single bad epoch. Out of eclipse the star is quiet (quiet_ratio 1.27). The eclipse is short (under a day) compared with the period, and the required speed is far below escape speed. All of this is consistent with stellar eclipses.

The star is also noisy otherwise (quiet_ratio 6.15, BP/RP scatter 5-7%), so a modest real low state may contribute, but an eclipse is weakly constrained and not required.
